Answer: D
Reason: The axial CT image (Figure 2) clearly demonstrates coarse, punctate calcifications within the large right-sided pleural mass. While primary lung cancers and metastases can occasionally calcify, prominent intratumoral calcification is a distinctive radiological feature often associated with pleuropulmonary synovial sarcoma, helping to distinguish it from other differentials.
